items.summary: Design the pages patient-flow leaders will open every morning: an Executive overview that shows Kestrel against its charter targets, and Site ED operations and Beds and flow pages that show where each site is under pressure. You pick each visual for the question it answers, format against triage objectives, and build accessibility and a phone layout in from the start.

read.heading: Start from the decision, not the visual
read.body:
Today you turn the semantic model into the pages that replace the emailed extracts. Before you place a visual, write down who opens each page and what they decide with it.

Release 1 serves three audiences through three main pages:

- Executive overview: executives such as Dr. Helen Marchetti (E-001) and Marcus Bell (E-002), with Janelle Cardinal (E-008), Director of Patient Flow. They ask: are we meeting the charter targets, which site is furthest off, and are beds the constraint?
- Site ED operations: site leaders such as Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007) and Aisha Mahmoud (E-010), Emergency Charge Nurse, at Kestrel General Hospital (KGH), and Dr. Liam O'Connor (E-012) at Aspen Ridge Hospital (ARH). They ask: which triage levels wait longest at my site, and when?
- Beds and flow: Janelle Cardinal and the patient-flow team. They ask: how full are the units, and how many alternate level of care (ALC) days are we carrying?

Hidden pages support them: Site detail for drillthrough and Site tooltip for hover detail. A Definitions and data notes page holds Kestrel's definitions, the last refresh time and the suppression rule.

Each question should trace to a line in the requirements and traceability register. A visual that answers no listed question goes, or its requirement goes through change control.

Use the five-second test: after five seconds a leader should be able to say what is on track and what is not. Put the most important number top left and keep each page to six to eight visuals.

Titles should state the point. Because the data refreshes daily, build them from a measure:

```
Wait Title =
"Median wait to physician: " & FORMAT ( [Median Minutes to PIA], "0.0" ) & " minutes"
```

Apply it with the fx button on the visual's title. Put the definition and period in the subtitle: "Arrival to physician initial assessment (PIA), 1 July to 30 September 2026".

read.heading: The Executive overview: four numbers against target
read.body:
The Executive overview opens with four cards across the top. Each card shows one measure from the Data Analysis Expressions (DAX) catalogue with its target and period. For the baseline, 1 July to 30 September 2026, the page must show:

| Card | Measure | Value | Target or context |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wait for a physician | Median Minutes to PIA | 80.5 minutes at KGH; 64.0 all sites | KGH target 60 (agreed) |
| Left without being seen (LWBS) | LWBS Rate | 5.7% all sites | 4.5% (agreed) |
| Bed occupancy | Occupancy % (Last Snapshot) | 84.0%: 121 of 144 staffed beds on 2026-09-30 | Period average 87.0% |
| Within triage objective | % PIA Within CTAS Target | 28.3% all sites (126 of 445) | KGH 12.8%, PGH 55.8% |

An LWBS visit is an emergency department (ED) visit that left before a physician initial assessment. CTAS is the Canadian Triage and Acuity Scale.

Two choices matter. The charter wait target applies to KGH only, so the card shows KGH against 60 with the all-sites median as context. And occupancy has two honest answers: the last snapshot (how full at the end) and the average of daily ratios (how full across the period). Show the snapshot on the card and the average in the subtitle, both labelled.

Below the cards, a bar chart compares median minutes to PIA by site, longest first: KGH 80.5, ARH 54.5, Coulee Valley Hospital (CVH) 54.0, Prairie Gate Health Centre (PGH) 45.5, with a constant line at 60 labelled "KGH target (agreed)". A weekly trend line of the median wait, a bar chart of occupancy by site (average daily: KGH 89.3%, ARH 84.8%, CVH 87.9%, PGH 76.8%) and a matrix of admitted visits by site with a total complete the page. The matrix uses ED Visits (Shared Total) from the DAX catalogue, so PGH shows "<5" and the total of 59 stays blank (test SUP-07). ALC patient-days (2,075, which is 18.4% of occupied bed-days) belong on Beds and flow, with occupancy by unit and the last-snapshot cards.

read.heading: Choose the visual for the question
read.body:
Pick the visual from the verb in the question:

| The question asks for | Use | Beacon example |
|---|---|---|
| One number against a goal | Card or key performance indicator (KPI) visual | LWBS rate against 4.5% |
| A comparison | Bar chart, sorted | Median wait by site |
| Change over time | Line chart | Daily occupancy |
| Parts of a whole | 100% stacked bar | Dispositions by site |
| Detail across two dimensions | Matrix | Triage level by site |
| A relationship | Scatter chart | Unit occupancy against ALC days |

Avoid crowded pie charts, 3D effects and misleading dual axes. Use the median for waits, because a few very long waits pull an average up.

A visual calculation is a DAX calculation that lives inside one visual and works on the data already in it: the quickest way to add a running total or moving average without a model measure. On the daily occupancy line chart, select New visual calculation and enter:

```
Occupancy 7-day average = MOVINGAVERAGE ( [Occupancy % (Average Daily)], 7 )
```

RUNNINGSUM and PREVIOUS are other visual calculation functions. Because a visual calculation exists only in its visual, use a model measure when the logic is needed on several pages or must be reconciled in the DAX catalogue.

read.heading: Conditional formatting against triage objectives
read.body:
The Canadian Triage and Acuity Scale (CTAS) sets a time-to-physician objective for each level: Level I Resuscitation immediate, Level II Emergent 15 minutes, Level III Urgent 30, Level IV Less Urgent 60, Level V Non Urgent 120. The CTAS guidelines call these objectives, not established care standards, so label them that way. DimCTAS[TargetMinutes] already holds them.

On Site ED operations, a matrix shows each CTAS level with visits, Median Minutes to PIA and % PIA Within CTAS Target. Colour the median against the objective:

```
PIA Status Colour =
VAR MedianWait = [Median Minutes to PIA]
VAR Objective = SELECTEDVALUE ( DimCTAS[TargetMinutes] )
RETURN
    SWITCH (
        TRUE (),
        ISBLANK ( MedianWait ) || ISBLANK ( Objective ), BLANK (),
        MedianWait <= Objective, "#2166AC",
        "#B35806"
    )
```

Apply it through Conditional formatting, Background colour, Format style Field value. A second measure, PIA Status, uses the same test to return "Within objective" or "Over objective"; add it as a column.

For all sites, the medians for Levels I to V are 1.0, 27.0, 55.0, 76.0 and 100.0 minutes, so only Level V is within its objective. % within target runs 42.9%, 33.3%, 15.6%, 30.5% and 58.9%. CTAS also sets fractile goals; the confirmed ones are 95% for Level II and 80% for Level V, so show only those two as reference values.

read.heading: Accessibility is part of the design
read.body:
The dashboards must work for people with low vision or colour vision deficiency, and for keyboard and screen-reader users.

- Contrast: text needs at least 4.5:1 against its background, and large text and chart marks at least 3:1 (the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) level AA rule). On white, #2166AC scores 5.9:1 and #B35806 scores 4.87:1, so both pass for text. A bright blue such as #118DFF scores 3.35:1 and yellow #FFB900 only 1.72:1, so neither works for small text.
- Never rely on colour alone. The blue and orange above differ in hue, but against each other they score only 1.21:1, so in greyscale they look almost the same. That is why the matrix carries the PIA Status words.
- Alt text: give every visual alt text (Format, General, Alt text) that says what it shows and the main finding. Alt text can come from a measure, so it stays true after each refresh.
- Tab order: in the Selection pane, match the tab order to the reading order and drop decorative shapes from it.
- A table alternative: every visual must still read correctly with Show as a table, which any viewer can use.

Put the accessible colours in a report theme so every page uses the same set.

read.heading: Phone layout, and when a paginated report fits
read.body:
Charge nurses such as Aisha Mahmoud check their site during a shift, often on a phone, so Site ED operations gets a phone layout. In Power BI Desktop, open that page, choose View, Mobile layout and drag visuals onto the phone canvas. It reuses the visuals already on the page, and larger screens keep the desktop layout. Place the CTAS table first, then length of stay and the weekly LWBS rate, one under another.

A paginated report, built in Power BI Report Builder, is designed to print or export: fixed layout, pages, and every row of a table however long. Use one when the requirement says print, PDF, exact layout or every row. A monthly quality-committee pack with one page per site, in the same layout each month, fits. Daily exploration by leaders does not; that is the interactive report's job.

Format never overrides privacy. Beacon's pages use de-identified, aggregated data classified Confidential, so a request for a printable list of individual patients is a privacy question first. The Health Information Act (HIA) requires the highest degree of anonymity possible and the least amount of information needed (sections 57 and 58), and Kestrel's own reporting rule suppresses counts under 5 in any report shared outside the care team.

keyTerms.definition: A design check: after five seconds on a page, a viewer should be able to say what is on track and what is not. If they cannot, the page has too many visuals or unclear titles.
A DAX calculation defined inside one visual that works on the data already in that visual, such as MOVINGAVERAGE or RUNNINGSUM. It is not stored as a model measure.
A conditional formatting style in which a measure returns the colour code to use, so the rule, such as median wait against the CTAS objective, lives in DAX and is easy to test.
The difference in luminance between text or a chart mark and its background. WCAG level AA asks for 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text and graphics.
A phone-shaped canvas in Power BI Desktop where you arrange visuals that already exist on a page, so the Power BI mobile app shows a portrait version of that page.
A fixed-layout report built in Power BI Report Builder for printing or PDF. It renders every row across as many pages as needed, which an interactive report does not.

build.goal: Design the Executive overview, Site ED operations and Beds and flow pages in the Executive and site operations reports document, with every visual tied to a leader's question and every value reconciled to truth.json.
steps: Open Project, Release 1, Executive and site operations reports. Read How to write it and See the finished example, then list the audience and three to five questions for each page.
Build the Executive overview cards: Median Minutes to PIA filtered to KGH, % PIA Within CTAS Target, LWBS Rate and Occupancy % (Last Snapshot). Check they read 80.5, 28.3%, 5.7% and 84.0%.

Add the median-wait bar chart by site, sorted longest first, with a constant line at 60 minutes labelled as the agreed KGH target, then the weekly trend line and occupancy by site. Confirm KGH 80.5, ARH 54.5, CVH 54.0 and PGH 45.5.

Build Site ED operations (the CTAS matrix with PIA Status Colour and PIA Status, length of stay admitted against discharged, LWBS rate by week) and Beds and flow (occupancy by unit, where KGH-MED4A should read 94.7%, the last-snapshot cards, ALC days by site, and the daily occupancy line with the 7-day moving-average visual calculation).
Apply the accessible colours through a theme, write alt text for every visual, set the tab order in the Selection pane, and replace field-name titles with measure-driven titles.
Arrange Site ED operations in Mobile layout: the CTAS table first, then length of stay and the weekly LWBS rate.

In the writing area, record each page's questions, visuals, expected values, your paginated report decision and the privacy rules. Tick the Done when list and write your explanation in Explain it in your own words.
build.modelAnswer: Executive overview, question 1: is KGH on track for the physician wait target? Visual: card, Median Minutes to PIA filtered to KGH, 80.5 minutes; subtitle 'Arrival to PIA, 1 July to 30 September 2026; target 60 (agreed)'. Question 2: which site is furthest off? Visual: bar chart sorted longest first (KGH 80.5, ARH 54.5, CVH 54.0, PGH 45.5) with a constant line at 60. Alt text: 'Median minutes from arrival to physician initial assessment by site; KGH longest at 80.5.' Paginated report: not needed for Release 1; reconsider if the quality committee asks for a fixed monthly PDF.

examTips.tip: Visual-choice questions turn on the verb: compare (bar), change over time (line), relationship (scatter), one value against a goal (card or KPI). If the colour must follow a rule held in a measure, the answer is conditional formatting with Field value.
A visual calculation adds logic such as RUNNINGSUM or MOVINGAVERAGE to one visual only. If the scenario needs the logic in several visuals or reused by other reports, choose a model measure instead.
When a requirement mentions printing, PDF, an exact page layout or exporting every row, the answer is a paginated report. Interactive exploration points to a standard Power BI report.
Process task 3, Help ensure value-based delivery: report design starts from the stakeholder's decision and the acceptance criteria in the requirements register, not from what the tool can draw.

pitfalls: Averaging the four site medians to get an all-sites figure. That gives 58.6 minutes; the median across all 445 visits with a valid PIA is 64.0.
Using colour alone for status. Add words or icons, because a colour-blind viewer or a greyscale print loses the meaning.
Drawing KGH's 60-minute target across every site as if it applied to them all. The charter target is for KGH; label the line.
Packing fifteen visuals onto one page. Each adds a query and splits attention; six to eight is a sensible ceiling.

check.q: Janelle asks whether KGH is on track for the charter wait target. What exactly does the card show?
check.a: Median Minutes to PIA filtered to KGH: 80.5 minutes from arrival to physician initial assessment for 1 July to 30 September 2026, with the agreed target of 60 minutes beside it. It is 20.5 minutes over target, and the card says so in words as well as colour.

check.q: Why does the occupancy card show 84.0% when the period average is 87.0%?
check.a: They answer different questions. 84.0% is the last snapshot: 121 occupied of 144 staffed beds on 2026-09-30. 87.0% is the average of the daily occupancy ratios across the quarter. The card shows the snapshot labelled 'as at 30 September', and the subtitle gives the period average.

check.q: Your CTAS matrix colours over-objective cells orange and within-objective cells blue. Is that enough for accessibility?
check.a: No. Both colours pass text contrast on white (4.87:1 and 5.9:1), but against each other they score only 1.21:1, so they look alike in greyscale and can confuse some colour-blind viewers. Add the PIA Status words, give the matrix alt text, and place it sensibly in the tab order.

items.summary: Connect the pages so each one answers the next question: drill through from a site on the Executive overview to the hidden Site detail page, show a site's key figures in a report page tooltip, swap occupancy views with bookmarks, and keep site and month choices in step with sync slicers.

read.heading: Navigation should follow the leader's next question
read.body:
Yesterday's pages answer the first question: where are we off target? The next question is why. Navigation features exist to get a leader from the first answer to the second without hunting.

Map each feature to a question before you build it:

| Leader's next question | Feature | Beacon use |
|---|---|---|
| Why is this site off target? | Drillthrough | From a site bar to the hidden Site detail page for that site |
| What sits behind this bar? | Report page tooltip | Hover a site to see its visits, wait, % within target and LWBS rate |
| Which occupancy answer do I need? | Bookmarks | Swap average daily and last snapshot occupancy |
| Can I keep my site and month? | Sync slicers | Site and month in step across pages |

Also decide how visuals on one page affect each other. Select a visual, then Format, Edit interactions: each other visual shows filter, highlight or none. On the Executive overview, a click on a site bar should filter the four cards to that site, so its wait, left without being seen (LWBS) rate and occupancy appear together.

Every feature must work with row-level security (RLS). A leader at Kestrel General Hospital (KGH) whose role shows only KGH data can drill only into KGH, and every tooltip and bookmark shows only rows the role allows. RLS filters the semantic model itself, so navigation cannot reveal another site's numbers.

read.heading: Drillthrough from a site to Site detail
read.body:
Drillthrough lets a user jump from a data point to a detail page filtered to that data point.

1. Add a page named Site detail and hide it, so users reach it only by drillthrough. With no visual selected, find the Drill through section of the Visualizations pane and drag DimSite[SiteCode] into it. The page becomes a drillthrough target and Power BI adds a back button at the top left.
2. Decide Keep all filters. On means every filter on the source page, such as a month or a triage level, travels with the user. Off means only the site travels. For Beacon keep it on so the month stays the same, and test that it carries nothing you did not intend.
3. On the Executive overview, right-click the KGH bar and choose Drill through, Site detail. The page opens for KGH only: 213 visits, a median of 80.5 minutes to physician initial assessment (PIA), 12.8% within the Canadian Triage and Acuity Scale (CTAS) target, LWBS rate 7.5%, and a median emergency department (ED) length of stay (LOS) of 15.14 hours for admitted patients against 4.30 hours for discharged patients.
4. Right-click is hidden from many users, so add a button: Insert, Buttons, Blank, then set Action to Drill through and Destination to Site detail. The button stays disabled until the user selects one site. Set its disabled tooltip to "Select a site, then open its page".

Drillthrough can also work across reports (turn on Cross-report on the target page) when the reports share the same semantic model fields. Beacon keeps both pages in one report, so it does not need it.

read.heading: Report page tooltips
read.body:
A default tooltip lists the fields in the visual. A report page tooltip shows a small page you design, filtered to the data point under the pointer.

1. Add a page named Site tooltip. In the Format pane for the page, open Page information and turn on Allow use as tooltip. Under Canvas settings, set Type to Tooltip so the page is small.
2. Add one small table or multi-row card with four values: ED Visits (Shared), Median Minutes to PIA, % PIA Within CTAS Target and LWBS Rate (Shared).
3. Hide the page so it does not appear as a tab.
4. On the Executive overview site bar chart, open Format, General, Tooltips. Set Type to Report page and Page to Site tooltip.

Hover the Prairie Gate Health Centre (PGH) bar and the tooltip shows PGH figures only, such as a median of 45.5 minutes to PIA and 55.8% within target. Keep a tooltip to two or three visuals: it vanishes when the pointer moves, so it suits a quick check, not reading.

Do not put the only copy of important information in a tooltip. Touch-screen and screen-reader users reach tooltips less easily than mouse users. Anything a decision depends on must also be on the page or one drillthrough away.

Tooltips are outputs too, so the tooltip page uses the shared measures that suppress small counts; tomorrow's tests check it.

read.heading: Bookmarks and the Selection pane
read.body:
A bookmark saves the state of a report page so a user can return to it with one click. When you add one, choose what it captures:

- Data: filters, slicer selections, sort order and drill state.
- Display: which visuals are shown or hidden, and spotlight or focus mode.
- Current page: whether selecting the bookmark moves the user to this page.
- All visuals or Selected visuals: whether it affects the whole page or only the visuals you selected.

Beacon uses bookmarks to swap the occupancy visuals between the two honest answers from yesterday: Average daily and Last snapshot.

1. Place the last-snapshot occupancy visual over the average-daily one. In the Selection pane, group them, then hide the last-snapshot visual.
2. In the Bookmarks pane, add Average daily. Then show the last-snapshot visual, hide the average one, and add Last snapshot.
3. Turn off Data for both. If Data stays on, clicking Last snapshot resets the user's site and month slicers to whatever they were when you made the bookmark. That is the most common bookmark bug.
4. Add two buttons with Action set to Bookmark, or a bookmark navigator (Insert, Buttons, Navigator).

A Reset filters bookmark keeps Data on, because its job is to return every slicer to all sites and the full period. Viewers in the service can also save personal bookmarks.

The Selection pane does two more jobs: its layer order decides which visual sits on top where visuals overlap, and its tab order decides the keyboard sequence. They are separate lists, so set both.

read.heading: Sync slicers and filter scope
read.body:
Leaders expect the month they pick on the Executive overview to stay picked on Site ED operations. Sync slicers does this.

1. Put a month slicer (DimDate[MonthName], sorted by MonthNumber) on the Executive overview, and a site slicer (DimSite[SiteCode]) on Site ED operations.
2. Open View, Sync slicers. For each page the pane shows two boxes: sync applies the selection on that page, and visible shows the slicer there.
3. Sync the month slicer to Site ED operations and Beds and flow, and the site slicer to Beds and flow. Leave the site slicer off the Executive overview, which compares sites, and off Site detail, because drillthrough already sets the site.
4. If two different slicer visuals use the same field, give them the same group name under Advanced options so they stay in step.

Filters have three scopes in the Filters pane: this visual, this page and all pages. Use an all-pages filter for rules that apply everywhere, and lock or hide filters users must not change. A filter is not security. Anyone who can edit the report, or build on the semantic model, can change or bypass it. RLS is the control that keeps sites apart.

With RLS in place, a site slicer lists only the sites the viewer's role allows: a KGH leader sees one value, KGH, while the All sites role sees all four.

read.heading: Test the navigation before you call it done
read.body:
Run these checks and record each result in the document:

1. Drill through from each site bar. Each site page shows that site's visits: KGH 213, Aspen Ridge Hospital (ARH) 105, Coulee Valley Hospital (CVH) 101, PGH 55. The back button returns to the Executive overview with the user's filters intact.
2. Set the month slicer to August, then drill through. The site page still shows August only.
3. Hover each site bar. The tooltip shows only that site.
4. Choose a site and a month, then press Last snapshot and Average daily. The slicers do not change.
5. Press Reset filters. Every slicer returns to all sites and all months.
6. Tab through the page with the keyboard only. The order follows the reading order, and every button can be reached and used. While editing in Power BI Desktop, hold Ctrl and click to test a button.
7. Open the Site ED operations phone layout. The CTAS table and charts still read clearly.

Fix each failure before tomorrow's testing session. A navigation defect found today costs minutes; one found by Janelle Cardinal at the morning bed meeting costs trust.

keyTerms.definition: A link from a data point on one page to a detail page filtered to that data point. The drillthrough field is placed on the target page, which gets a back button.
A drillthrough setting that carries every filter from the source page to the target page, not only the drillthrough field. Useful, but test it for filters you did not intend.
A small report page, set to Allow use as tooltip, that appears when a user hovers over a data point and is filtered to that point.
A saved state of a report page. Its Data, Display and Current page options decide whether it restores filters, visibility of visuals, and which page is shown.
The pane that lists every visual on a page, where you show, hide and group visuals, set the layer order, and set the keyboard tab order.
A pane that makes one slicer's selection apply on other pages (sync) and controls whether the slicer appears there (visible). Slicer groups keep different slicers on one field in step.
A setting for how a selection in one visual affects each other visual on the page: filter, highlight, or no effect.

build.goal: Add drillthrough, a report page tooltip, occupancy bookmarks and synced slicers to the Executive and site operations reports, and record a navigation map and test results in the document.
steps: Open Project, Release 1, Executive and site operations reports, and add a Navigation section to your writing: one row per feature with the question it answers.
Make the hidden Site detail page a drillthrough target on DimSite[SiteCode] with Keep all filters on, and add a drillthrough button with a disabled-state tooltip on the Executive overview.
Build the Site tooltip page (tooltip canvas, Allow use as tooltip on, page hidden) and assign it to the site bar charts.
Create Average daily and Last snapshot bookmarks with Data turned off, a Reset filters bookmark with Data on, and a bookmark navigator.
Sync the month slicer across Executive overview, Site ED operations and Beds and flow, and the site slicer across Site ED operations and Beds and flow, keeping it off Site detail.
Use Edit interactions so a click on the site bar filters the four cards to that site.
Run the seven navigation tests, record pass or fail with the values you saw, and compare your document with See the finished example.
build.modelAnswer: Navigation map (extract). Drillthrough: Executive overview site bar to Site detail on DimSite[SiteCode], Keep all filters on. Test: KGH shows 213 visits and 80.5 minutes; August filter kept; back button returns. Tooltip: Site tooltip on the site bar charts. Test: PGH hover shows PGH only, 45.5 minutes and 55.8%. Bookmarks: Average daily and Last snapshot with Data off; Reset filters with Data on. Test: the swap leaves slicers unchanged. Sync slicers: month synced on Executive overview, Site ED operations and Beds and flow; site synced on Site ED operations and Beds and flow, not on Site detail. Result: 7 of 7 tests passed.

examTips.tip: For drillthrough, the drillthrough field goes on the target (detail) page, not the source page. Power BI adds the back button to the target page for you.
If a bookmark must not change the user's current filters, turn off its Data option. If it must reset filters, keep Data on. Scenario questions often test exactly this choice.
Sync slicers has two settings per page: sync (the selection applies) and visible (the slicer shows). Different slicer visuals on the same field stay in step through a shared group name.
A report page tooltip needs two settings: Allow use as tooltip on the tooltip page, and Type set to Report page in the target visual's tooltip options.

pitfalls: Leaving Data on in a view-toggle bookmark, so every click resets the leader's site and month.
Treating a hidden or locked filter as security. Only RLS keeps one site's rows away from another site's leaders.
Putting key facts only in a tooltip, where touch-screen and screen-reader users may never see them.
Forgetting that Keep all filters carries every source filter, including a triage level the user clicked earlier.

check.q: A leader clicks Last snapshot and her month slicer jumps back to July. What went wrong and how do you fix it?
check.a: The bookmark was saved with Data turned on, so it reapplies the slicer state from when it was made. Turn off Data for Average daily and Last snapshot so they change only which visuals are displayed. Keep Data on only for the Reset filters bookmark.

check.q: Where does DimSite[SiteCode] go to make drillthrough work, and what does the user see when drilling from the KGH bar?
check.a: It goes in the Drill through section of the hidden Site detail page, the target. Drilling from KGH opens that page filtered to KGH: 213 visits, 80.5 median minutes to PIA, 12.8% within CTAS target, LWBS rate 7.5%, and admitted LOS of 15.14 hours against 4.30 hours for discharged patients.

check.q: Could a KGH leader use a tooltip or drillthrough to see Aspen Ridge figures?
check.a: No. RLS filters the semantic model itself, so every visual, tooltip page and drillthrough page is evaluated inside the KGH role. The site slicer lists only KGH and drillthrough can only reach KGH. You still prove this with negative RLS tests rather than assuming it.

items.summary: Prove the release is right, usable, fast and safe before anyone relies on it. You reconcile every visual to truth.json with Data Analysis Expressions (DAX) queries, test accessibility the way users work, time each visual with Performance Analyzer, and run positive and negative row-level security tests, including the small-count suppression that is the go-live condition.

read.heading: Four claims, four kinds of evidence
read.body:
Release 1 goes live only if four claims can be proved, not asserted:

| Claim | Test | Evidence goes in |
|---|---|---|
| The numbers are right | Reconcile every visual to truth.json | Quality plan |
| Everyone can use it | Accessibility checks | Quality plan |
| It is fast enough | Performance Analyzer timings | Quality plan |
| Each site sees only its own data | Positive and negative row-level security (RLS) tests | RLS test pack |

Write every test the same way: ID, what is tested, expected result, actual result, pass or fail, evidence (a screenshot or query output), tester and date. Write the expected result before you run the test. A test written after you see the answer only describes what happened.

The figures below are the approved baseline for 1 July to 30 September 2026: emergency department (ED) visits, minutes to physician initial assessment (PIA), the left without being seen (LWBS) rate, bed occupancy and alternate level of care (ALC) days. Sites are Kestrel General Hospital (KGH), Aspen Ridge Hospital (ARH), Coulee Valley Hospital (CVH) and Prairie Gate Health Centre (PGH).

In PMP terms this is Process task 7, Plan and optimize quality of products/deliverables. In CISSP terms it is Domain 6, Security Assessment and Testing.

read.heading: Accuracy: reconcile in DAX query view
read.body:
Open DAX query view in Power BI Desktop and run one DAX query per visual family. This one reproduces the site comparison:

```
EVALUATE
SUMMARIZECOLUMNS (
    DimSite[SiteCode],
    "ED Visits", [ED Visits],
    "Median Minutes to PIA", [Median Minutes to PIA],
    "Pct Within Target", [% PIA Within CTAS Target],
    "LWBS Rate", [LWBS Rate],
    "Occupancy Avg", [Occupancy % (Average Daily)],
    "ALC Days", [ALC Days]
)
ORDER BY DimSite[SiteCode]
```

| Site | Visits | Median min to PIA | Within target | LWBS rate | Occupancy avg | ALC days |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ARH | 105 | 54.5 | 34.0% | 4.8% | 84.8% | 561 |
| CVH | 101 | 54.0 | 39.2% | 4.0% | 87.9% | 377 |
| KGH | 213 | 80.5 | 12.8% | 7.5% | 89.3% | 835 |
| PGH | 55 | 45.5 | 55.8% | 3.6% | 76.8% | 302 |

Then check the grand totals:

```
EVALUATE
ROW (
    "ED Visits", [ED Visits],
    "Median Minutes to PIA", [Median Minutes to PIA],
    "LWBS Rate", [LWBS Rate],
    "Occupancy Last", [Occupancy % (Last Snapshot)],
    "ALC Days", [ALC Days]
)
```

Expected: 474, 64.0, 5.7%, 84.0% and 2,075. Round before you compare. Two traps confirm the model is right: the all-sites median is 64.0, not the average of the site medians (58.6), and summing StaffedBeds over every row gives 12,952 bed-days, while Kestrel had 144 staffed beds on 2026-09-30. Finally compare every visual with the query output. A visual that disagrees has a filter, interaction or visual-level setting the query does not.

read.heading: Performance: Performance Analyzer and DAX query view
read.body:
Performance Analyzer records how long each visual takes. Open the Performance Analyzer pane, select Start recording, then Refresh visuals. Each visual gets a line split three ways:

- DAX query: time for the semantic model to answer. A slow measure or a poor relationship shows here.
- Visual display: time to draw the result. Too many data points or a heavy visual shows here.
- Other: time spent waiting, often for other visuals on the page. Many visuals push this up.

Copy the query of the slowest visual and paste it into DAX query view. There you can run it alone and try a rewritten measure without changing the model:

```
DEFINE
    MEASURE FactEDVisit[LWBS Visits Test] =
        CALCULATE ( [ED Visits], FactEDVisit[Disposition] = "LWBS" )
EVALUATE
SUMMARIZECOLUMNS ( DimSite[SiteCode], "LWBS Visits", [LWBS Visits Test] )
```

Beacon's model is small (474 visits, 643 census rows, 219 tickets), so every visual will be quick. Record the timings anyway: they are the baseline for when data grows or someone adds a heavy visual. The agreed quality-plan target (quality gate QG-4) is that every visual renders in 3 seconds or less in Performance Analyzer. Usual fixes when a visual misses: fewer visuals per page, filtering a column rather than a whole table inside CALCULATE, removing unused columns, and reducing granularity.

read.heading: Accessibility: test it the way users work
read.body:
Test with the methods people use:

1. Keyboard only. Put the mouse away and tab through each page. Focus follows the tab order you set, and every button can be reached and used.
2. Screen reader. Each visual announces useful alt text, such as "Median minutes to physician initial assessment by site; KGH longest at 80.5". Show as a table reads as a table.
3. Contrast. Text is at least 4.5:1 against its background. Beacon's theme uses #252423 for text (15.49:1 on white), #2166AC (5.9:1) and #B35806 (4.87:1).
4. No colour. View the page in greyscale. Every status still reads, because the triage matrix says Within objective or Over objective in words.
5. Phone. Open the Site ED operations mobile layout in the Power BI mobile app and read every visual without zooming.

Log each check as pass or fail with a note. A fail is a defect with an owner and a fix date, like any other defect.

read.heading: Access: positive and negative RLS tests
read.body:
Beacon has a role for each site plus All sites for executives and patient-flow leaders. A positive test proves a role sees what it should. A negative test proves it cannot see what it should not. Negative tests are the ones that find leaks.

In Desktop use Modeling, View as and pick a role (for a dynamic role, also enter Other user). In the service, open the semantic model's Security page and use Test as role.

| Role | Visits | Median min to PIA | Occupancy avg | Staffed beds 2026-09-30 | ALC days |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Site KGH | 213 | 80.5 | 89.3% | 72 | 835 |
| Site ARH | 105 | 54.5 | 84.8% | 40 | 561 |
| Site CVH | 101 | 54.0 | 87.9% | 22 | 377 |
| Site PGH | 55 | 45.5 | 76.8% | 10 | 302 |
| All sites | 474 | 64.0 | 87.0% | 144 | 2,075 |

Negative tests for each site role:

- The site slicer lists one site, and totals equal that site (KGH shows 213, never 474).
- Beds and flow lists only that site's units. KGH shows KGH-MED4A, KGH-SUR5B and KGH-ICU and nothing from ARH, which proves the filter reaches FactBedCensus through DimUnit.
- Drillthrough, tooltips and Show as a table show no other site.
- A user in no role sees no data.

One test is about people, not DAX. RLS applies only to Viewers and app users; workspace Admins, Members and Contributors see every row. Check the workspace membership list: no site leader may hold Member or Contributor.

read.heading: Small-count suppression: the go-live condition
read.body:
Kestrel's reporting rule (Kestrel policy) suppresses counts under 5 in any report shared outside the care team. It puts into practice the Health Information Act duty to use the highest degree of anonymity possible and the least amount of information needed (sections 57 and 58). Risk R-02 names PGH, with 55 valid visits in the quarter, as the site where small counts could identify patients. Go-live decision D-02 carries one condition: small-count suppression for PGH verified in the RLS test pack.

Your test query shows why. LWBS visits by site are KGH 16, ARH 5, CVH 4 and PGH 2, and PGH had only 4 admitted visits. The rule is about counts, not sites, so the CVH count of 4 is suppressed too.

Every shared page uses the shared measures from the DAX catalogue:

```
ED Visits (Shared) =
VAR Visits = [ED Visits]
RETURN
    IF ( ISBLANK ( Visits ), BLANK (), IF ( Visits < 5, "<5", FORMAT ( Visits, "#,0" ) ) )

LWBS Rate (Shared) =
VAR LWBSVisits =
    CALCULATE ( [ED Visits], FactEDVisit[Disposition] = "LWBS" )
RETURN
    IF ( LWBSVisits < 5, BLANK (), [LWBS Rate] )
```

Rates leak too: a PGH LWBS rate of 3.6% on 55 visits tells anyone with a calculator that 2 patients left. The same Kestrel policy blanks any rate whose numerator is under 5, which is what LWBS Rate (Shared) does, and a footnote explains that counts under 5 show as "<5". Medians are not suppressed by this rule. Totals can leak as well: if a table shows a total and every cell but one, subtraction reveals the hidden cell.

Add suppression cases SUP-01 to SUP-07 to the RLS test pack: under the Site PGH and All sites roles, the PGH LWBS and admitted counts show "<5", the PGH LWBS rate is blank, a count of exactly 5 still shows, the admitted total that would reveal PGH's 4 by subtraction is blank, and no tooltip or Show as a table view reveals the 2 or the 4.

keyTerms.definition: A view in Power BI Desktop where you write and run DAX queries such as EVALUATE SUMMARIZECOLUMNS, and define test measures, without changing the model.
A Power BI Desktop pane that records each visual's time split into DAX query, Visual display and Other, and lets you copy the visual's query.
Comparing a model or report result with an independently approved figure, such as truth.json, and explaining every difference before release.
A test that proves something is refused or hidden, such as a KGH role seeing no ARH rows. Negative tests find access leaks that positive tests miss.
A Power BI Desktop feature (Modeling, View as) that shows the report as a chosen RLS role, or as another user for dynamic roles, so you can test security before publishing.
Hiding counts below a threshold, under 5 at Kestrel, and any rate or total that would let someone work them out, so small groups of patients cannot be identified.

Domain 6, Security Assessment and Testing: a control is assured only by tests that try to break it. Expect the best answer to include negative tests and independent evidence, not a configuration screenshot alone.

pitfalls: Writing expected results after running the test, which turns a test into a description.
Testing RLS while signed in as a workspace Member, who sees every row anyway.
Suppressing the PGH count but not the PGH rate, which lets anyone recompute the count from 55 visits.
Comparing unrounded Power BI values with rounded truth figures and logging false failures.

check.q: Under the Site KGH role, Beds and flow still lists ARH Medicine. What does that tell you and where do you look?
check.a: The site filter is not reaching FactBedCensus. It travels through DimUnit, so check that DimSite[SiteCode] relates one-to-many to DimUnit[SiteCode] and DimUnit[UnitID] one-to-many to FactBedCensus[UnitID], with filters flowing towards the fact table. Under KGH you expect three units and 72 staffed beds on 2026-09-30.

check.q: A matrix total of median minutes to PIA reads 58.6. Is something wrong?
check.a: Yes. 58.6 is the average of the four site medians, so the total row is averaging site values instead of evaluating the measure. The Median Minutes to PIA measure in the total's filter context returns 64.0, the median of all 445 visits with a valid PIA. Look for an implicit average or a visual calculation over the site rows.

check.q: Why is a 3.6% LWBS rate for PGH a privacy problem, and what is the test?
check.a: PGH had 55 valid visits, so 3.6% reveals 2 LWBS visits, below Kestrel's threshold of 5. Under the Site PGH and All sites roles, test that the PGH LWBS count shows "<5", the rate is blank, and no tooltip or Show as a table view shows the 2. Passing this test is the D-02 condition.

items.summary: Plan how Release 1 runs in the Power BI service: who holds which workspace role, how leaders receive the reports through an app, how the semantic model refreshes from the on-premises warehouse through a gateway, how content is labelled and endorsed, and how a change is deployed, checked and rolled back.

read.heading: Workspaces and the four roles
read.body:
A workspace is where content is built and managed. Beacon uses three: Beacon Dev, Beacon Test and Beacon Prod. Each person or group gets one of four roles:

| Role | Can do | Row-level security (RLS) |
|---|---|---|
| Admin | Everything, including adding Admins and deleting the workspace | Sees all rows |
| Member | Add people with lower roles, publish and update the app, share | Sees all rows |
| Contributor | Create, edit and publish content; update the app only if an Admin allows it | Sees all rows |
| Viewer | View and interact with content | RLS applies |

The last column is the security point. Only Viewers and app users are filtered by RLS, so site leaders must never hold Member or Contributor in Beacon Prod.

Beacon's assignments: Tomás Rivera (E-006) is Admin of all three. Mei Tanaka (E-013) and Lumen Analytics Partners (V-05) are Contributors in Beacon Dev; Lumen's role ends with their contract on 2026-11-30 (risk R-07). A second Prod admin is needed for key-person risk R-06, but an admin sees every site, so it stays pending until a second builder is named and Janelle Cardinal (E-008) approves all-site access for that person. Mei Tanaka holds no workspace role in Beacon Prod: there she uses the app as a Viewer in the Site CVH RLS role, so RLS applies, and her excess "view all sites" grant has been removed (SAC-06). User acceptance testers are Viewers in Beacon Test. No one holds Member in any Beacon workspace, and Beacon Prod has no Viewers: leaders receive the app.

Assign roles to security groups from the Identity Directory (A-007), not to named individuals. When someone joins or leaves, the group changes once and every workspace follows. Release 2 will drive those groups from human resources (HR) events.

read.heading: Distribute through an app
read.body:
An app packages content from one workspace for a wider audience. It suits Beacon because leaders get a stable, curated view and building stays separate from consuming.

- Audiences: one app can have several audiences, each seeing chosen reports and pages. Beacon's app, Beacon Patient Flow, has two: Executive (all pages) and Site operations (every page except the Executive overview), each fed by Identity Directory groups. Audiences decide which content people see; RLS decides which rows. You need both.
- Release control: report changes in the workspace reach app users only when you select Update app. The app reads the workspace's semantic model directly, though, so a model change reaches users at once. Test model changes in Beacon Test first.
- Build permission on the semantic model lets people create their own reports and query the model, for example from Excel. Give it only to analysts who need it. Their RLS role still applies.

| Method | Fits when | Beacon |
|---|---|---|
| App | Many consumers, curated content | Main route |
| Direct sharing | A few people, one item | Off; hard to audit |
| Teams or SharePoint | Leaders work in Teams | Possible later |
| Subscriptions | A page snapshot by email | Optional |
| Publish to web | Public data only | Never |

Publish to web creates a link anyone can open without signing in, so it must be off for Confidential content. Beacon turns it off; access is through the app only.

read.heading: Scheduled refresh and when a gateway is required
read.body:
Beacon's semantic model uses Import mode: data is copied into the model and refreshed on a schedule. Its source is the de-identified views in the Clinical Data Warehouse (A-010), which is on premises. The Power BI service runs in the cloud and cannot reach that source by itself, so an on-premises data gateway is required.

A gateway is needed when an Import model refreshes from a source inside Kestrel's network, or when a DirectQuery or live connection reaches such a source. It is not needed for cloud sources the service can reach directly.

Use standard mode. Personal mode serves one user and supports Import only, which is wrong for a shared service. Install two gateway members as a cluster so a server patch does not stop refresh, and keep the recovery key in a secure vault. The gateway makes outbound connections only, so no inbound firewall port opens, but Ahmed Haddad (E-017) must still allow its outbound traffic. Its data source uses a service account with read-only rights on the de-identified views and nothing else. The credentials are encrypted, stored in the gateway cloud service and decrypted only on the gateway.

Schedule: daily at 05:00 (agreed), so dashboards show yesterday's data by 06:00, before the morning bed meeting. Shared capacity allows up to 8 scheduled refreshes a day; Premium or Fabric capacity allows 48. Send failure notifications to the Analytics Support mailbox, not one person, so the service desk hears of a failure within 1 hour. Power BI pauses scheduled refresh after two months with no use of the model, so the service owner needs to know. Add a "Data as at" card showing the latest census date, so a failed refresh is visible to every leader.

read.heading: Sensitivity labels and endorsement
read.body:
Kestrel classifies the Beacon dashboards as Confidential: de-identified, aggregated data. Show that in the service with a sensitivity label from Microsoft Purview Information Protection.

- A label applies to an item: a semantic model, report, dashboard or dataflow. It does not apply to a column, and the app itself is not labelled. It classifies the whole item.
- Labels flow. With downstream inheritance, a report built on the labelled semantic model gets the label. Exports to Excel, PowerPoint and PDF carry the label, and any protection set in the label travels with the file. Exports to .csv do not carry it, so Beacon turns .csv export off.
- A label does not grant or block access inside the service. Access comes from workspace roles, app audiences and RLS. The label tells people how to handle the content and protects exported copies.

Apply Confidential to the semantic model and the reports, and record it in the health information classification register.

Endorsement tells people which content to trust:

- Promoted: anyone with write access to the item can promote it, meaning it is ready to use.
- Certified: only reviewers the Power BI administrator authorizes can certify it, meaning it meets the organization's quality standard.

Certify the Beacon semantic model once its tests pass, so analysts build on the trusted model instead of making copies with their own definitions.

read.heading: Deployment and rollback
read.body:
Content moves from Beacon Dev to Beacon Test to Beacon Prod. A deployment pipeline in the service does this stage by stage and shows what differs between stages. Pipelines need the workspaces on a capacity (Premium Per User, Premium or Fabric). Deployment rules swap stage-specific settings, such as a data source rule: Beacon Dev uses test views, and the rule points Beacon Test and Beacon Prod at the live de-identified views, so release checks run against the approved figures.

Every Beacon Prod deployment needs:

1. A normal change in the IT Service Management Platform (A-011), approved by Marcus Bell (E-002) or his delegate, with the test evidence attached.
2. A window away from the 05:00 refresh and the morning bed meeting, such as Tuesday 18:00 to 19:00 (proposed).
3. A smoke test afterwards: the refresh succeeds, and each page opened as one site role and as an executive shows the five headline values from the test results.
4. An app update, the moment users see report changes.

Rollback means returning to the last version that passed its tests. Keep each released version as a Power BI project (.pbip) in version control, tagged by release. If the smoke test fails, do not update the app; redeploy the tagged version. The proposed target is the last approved version restored within 2 hours. The asset register gives A-009 a recovery time objective (RTO) of 72 hours and a recovery point objective (RPO) of 24 hours, so a same-day rollback sits well inside its targets.

read.heading: Monitoring and the handover to support
read.body:
After go-live, someone must notice problems before leaders do. Plan it now:

| What | How | Who acts |
|---|---|---|
| Refresh failed | Failure notification within 1 hour; refresh history each morning | Analytics Support |
| Gateway offline | Gateway status in the service | Ahmed Haddad (E-017) |
| Wrong numbers | Smoke test after each deployment | Tomás Rivera (E-006) |
| Low use | Usage metrics, monthly; unused pages go to the service review | Tomás Rivera (E-006) |
| Unexpected exports or role changes | Activity log, monthly | Sam Okafor (E-020) |

Record the configuration items a change can break: the three workspaces, the app and its audiences, the semantic model and its RLS roles, the gateway cluster and data source, the service account, and the label. Together they make up A-009, the Power BI service and Beacon semantic model.

In ITIL terms you are preparing the Transition stage: the service is built and must move into Operate, Deliver and Support with changes controlled and knowledge in place. In CISSP terms (Domain 7, Security Operations) this is configuration management and change management. Tomorrow you hand all of it to Grace Liu (E-005), the service owner, and her service desk, so write it for someone who was not in the room when it was built.

keyTerms.definition: One of Admin, Member, Contributor or Viewer, setting what a person can do in a workspace. Only Viewers (and app users) are filtered by row-level security.
A group of app users who see a chosen set of reports and pages. Audiences control which content is visible; RLS still controls which rows.
Software installed inside Kestrel's network that lets the Power BI service refresh from, or query, on-premises sources such as A-010. Standard mode is the shared, clusterable version.
A Microsoft Purview classification applied to whole items such as semantic models and reports. It flows to downstream items and exported files; it does not apply to columns.
A trust marker on content: Promoted by anyone with write access, or Certified by reviewers the administrator authorizes.
A Power BI service feature that moves content between stages such as Development, Test and Production, with rules to change data sources or parameters per stage.
Permission on a semantic model that lets a user create new content on it and query it from tools such as Excel, still within their RLS role.

App audiences control which content a group sees; RLS controls which rows. Report changes reach the app only after Update app, but the shared semantic model changes for app users immediately.

Expecting a sensitivity label on a column. Labels classify items; column exposure is handled by model design and RLS.
Assuming the app shields users from every change. Report changes wait for Update app; semantic model changes do not.

check.q: Why does Beacon need a gateway, and in which mode?
check.a: The semantic model imports from the Clinical Data Warehouse (A-010), which is on premises, and the cloud service cannot reach it directly. Use the on-premises data gateway in standard mode, clustered for availability, because personal mode serves one user, supports only Import and is not suitable for a shared service.

check.q: Dr. Sarah Whitford is made a Beacon Prod workspace Member so she can share the report. What changes for her?
check.a: RLS stops applying to her, because it filters only Viewers and app users, so she now sees every row in the model. She also gains rights to change content. Give her the app with the right audience and RLS role instead, and keep Beacon Prod roles to the build team.

check.q: An administrator asks you to put the Confidential label on the MinutesToPIA column. What do you answer?
check.a: Sensitivity labels apply to items such as the semantic model and reports, not to columns. Apply Confidential to the Beacon semantic model and reports; it then flows to downstream reports and exported files. Which columns people can reach is decided by model design, permissions and RLS.

items.summary: Bring the evidence together and make the Release 1 go-live decision: go, go with conditions, or no-go. Then hand the analytics service to Grace Liu's service desk with knowledge articles, known errors with workarounds and a clear escalation path, so support works from the first morning.

read.heading: Decide on evidence, not on the date
read.body:
The Release 1 go-live gate is 2026-10-23. It sits on the critical path with zero float, straight after user acceptance testing (UAT) with emergency department (ED) and patient-flow leaders from 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-23. A fixed date pushes towards yes; your job is to make the decision rest on evidence anyone can inspect.

Who does what at the gate (Beacon governance):

- You, as Programme Manager, present the evidence and a recommendation.
- The business owners, Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007) for emergency data and Janelle Cardinal (E-008) for bed data, confirm the reports meet their acceptance criteria.
- Grace Liu (E-005), service owner and IT Service Desk Manager, accepts the service for support.
- Priya Raman (E-003), Chief Privacy Officer, verifies the privacy condition, small-count suppression, in the row-level security test pack.
- The sponsor, Dr. Helen Marchetti (E-001), decides.

Cost and schedule are reported, not used as the reason to go. At the as-of date 2026-10-01, Release 1 had a cost performance index (CPI) of 0.89 and a schedule performance index (SPI) of 0.89. They say the release is costing more and moving slower than planned, not whether the dashboards are safe to use.

read.heading: Readiness criteria and their evidence
read.body:
Each criterion names its evidence. If the evidence does not exist, the criterion is not met. Partial evidence is not met either: "row-level security (RLS) tested for three of four sites" is a fail.

| Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Leaders accept the reports | UAT sign-off by E-007 and E-008 against the requirements register |
| Numbers are right | Quality plan: every visual reconciled to truth.json (474 visits, 64.0 minutes, 5.7%, 84.0%, 2,075) |
| Each site sees only its data | RLS test pack: positive and negative tests for every role |
| Small counts suppressed | RLS test pack: counts under 5 hidden, including Prairie Gate Health Centre (PGH) and Coulee Valley Hospital (CVH) |
| Usable by everyone | Quality plan: keyboard, screen reader, contrast, greyscale, phone |
| Privacy assessed | Privacy impact assessment approved by Priya Raman (E-003) and submitted to the Commissioner |
| Security conditions met | Security acceptance criteria all observed |
| Runs in the service | Workspace plan: gateway, refresh, label, app, rollback tested |
| Supported | Desk acceptance, knowledge articles, escalation path |

The privacy row needs care. Under the Health Information Act, section 64, a custodian must submit a privacy impact assessment to the Information and Privacy Commissioner before it implements a new information system or practice involving individually identifying health information. The Commissioner reviews and comments; it does not approve. So the evidence is the submission before go-live, not an approval letter.

read.heading: Go, go with conditions, or no-go
read.body:
The decision has three possible outcomes:

- Go: every criterion is met.
- Go with conditions: a few criteria are not fully met, the remaining risk is understood and owned, and each gap can be closed and verified before anyone is exposed to it.
- No-go: a criterion that protects privacy, data accuracy or patient safety is not met and cannot be contained.

A condition is acceptable only if it is specific, testable, owned and dated, and the decision says what happens if it is not met. "Improve suppression" is not a condition. "Small-count suppression for PGH verified in the RLS test pack" is.

That is Beacon's decision D-02: Release 1 go-live approved on 2026-10-23 with one condition, small-count suppression for PGH verified in the RLS test pack. It passes the test. The risk is named (R-02, owned by Priya Raman, E-003), the fix is small (suppressed measures), and the test cases already exist from your testing session. In the go-live document, record who verifies the condition (Priya Raman), the evidence attached, and the consequence if it fails: the app opens to users on 2026-10-26, and if the condition is not verified by 08:00 that day, the app stays unpublished.

Write the decision record with date, decision, conditions, evidence references, decision maker and the risks accepted. A decision without a record cannot be audited later.

read.heading: Transition into operation and support
read.body:
ITIL Version 5 describes eight stages in the product and service lifecycle: Discover, Design, Acquire, Build, Transition, Operate, Deliver and Support. Release 1 has been in Build. Go-live is Transition: moving a tested change into live use without harming the service or its users. After it, the analytics service lives in Operate (refresh, the gateway and the workspaces monitored and maintained), Deliver (access requests handled, reports reaching leaders each morning, feedback collected) and Support (incidents and problems resolved).

Transition is complete only when the people who run and support the service accept it, with their knowledge in place before the first call.

Plan a short period of early life support, often called hypercare: two weeks, 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-06, in which the Beacon team sits beside the service desk, answers escalations the same day and fixes defects quickly. End it on agreed exit criteria, not on the calendar: no open priority 1 or 2 incident, refresh on time on at least 9 of the 10 working days (proposed), a knowledge article for every ticket type seen, and the first service review held.

Two guiding principles apply. Collaborate and promote visibility: the desk co-writes the knowledge articles. Keep it simple and practical: three tiers with named contacts beat a matrix nobody reads.

read.heading: Known errors and knowledge articles
read.body:
ITIL separates an incident, an unplanned interruption to a service or reduction in its quality, from a problem, a cause or potential cause of one or more incidents. A known error is a problem that has been analysed but not resolved. A workaround reduces or removes the impact of an incident or problem while a full fix is not available. Known errors with workarounds let the desk resolve calls at first contact.

Beacon's known errors come straight from the data-quality findings:

| Known error | What users see | Workaround |
|---|---|---|
| ARH-SUR census missing for 2026-08-16 | Aspen Ridge Hospital (ARH) occupancy that day uses ARH Medicine only | Explain; snapshot requested from A-006 |
| CVH-MED alternate level of care (ALC) value for 2026-07-22 blanked | That unit-day shows no ALC count | Explain; unit is confirming the value |
| KGH-MED4A on 2026-09-08 | Occupancy above 100% (34 occupied, 32 staffed) | Not an error: surge beds, flagged |
| Visits V0070, V0222, V0476, V0075 quarantined | 474 valid visits, not 478 | Explain the rule; corrected at source |

Write knowledge articles for the calls you expect:

- "I can't see my site": check the app audience and the person's RLS group.
- "The numbers look old": check the Data as at card and the refresh history.
- "This doesn't match my Excel extract": explain Beacon's definitions, such as physician initial assessment (PIA) timed from arrival.
- "I need access to the dashboards": log an access request through the service desk.

Functional escalation moves a ticket to a group with the right skills; hierarchical escalation moves it up the management line. Two routes skip the tiers:

read.heading: Closing a release, not the programme
read.body:
Release 1 closes; Beacon does not. Closing a release means confirming its scope is accepted and handed over, and giving everything still open to a named owner.

Release 1 closure checklist:

- Acceptance: user acceptance testing (UAT) signed off and the D-02 condition verified and recorded.
- Handover: Grace Liu (E-005), the service owner, has accepted the service for support; knowledge articles and known errors are live.
- Benefits: the charter measures are taken three months after the release, on 2027-01-25 (2027-01-23 is a Saturday), which is after programme acceptance on 2026-12-17. So name business owners who will still be there: Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007) for the median minutes to physician initial assessment (PIA) at Kestrel General Hospital (KGH), baseline 80.5 and target 60 (agreed), and Janelle Cardinal (E-008) for the left without being seen (LWBS) rate, baseline 5.7% and target 4.5% (agreed).
- Open items: risks and issues move to the programme RAID (risks, assumptions, issues and decisions) log with owners. The Lumen Analytics Partners (V-05) contract stays open until 2026-11-30 (risk R-07), so plan their knowledge transfer now.
- Records: final versions of the Release 1 documents filed.

In PMP terms this is Process task 10, Manage project closure, applied to a release, and People task 7, Help ensure knowledge transfer.

read.heading: Release 1 in numbers
read.body:
Lessons need evidence, so start with the facts at the latest status date, 2026-10-01:

| Measure | Release 1 | Programme |
|---|---|---|
| Planned value (PV) | CAD 211,400 | CAD 278,900 |
| Earned value (EV) | CAD 188,000 | CAD 224,000 |
| Actual cost (AC) | CAD 211,000 | CAD 250,600 |
| Cost performance index (CPI) | 0.89 | 0.89 |
| Schedule performance index (SPI) | 0.89 | 0.80 |

Release 1 cost variance (EV minus AC) is CAD -23,000 and schedule variance (EV minus PV) is CAD -23,400. For the programme, the estimate at completion is CAD 1,342,500, a variance of CAD -142,500 against the CAD 1,200,000 budget. That is more than the CAD 120,000 management reserve, which is why risk R-08 exists.

Quality facts: of 480 emergency department (ED) source rows, 2 were duplicates and 4 were quarantined, leaving 474 valid visits. The bed census had one duplicate, one missing unit-day, one over-capacity row and one negative alternate level of care (ALC) value. All were found by profiling before modelling, and every figure reconciles to truth.json.

read.heading: Lessons that change behaviour
read.body:
A lesson is useful only if someone will act differently. Write each as: what happened, impact, root cause, recommendation, owner, and where it applies. Record what went well too.

Weak: "Privacy was hard." Strong: "Small-count suppression became a go-live condition (D-02) instead of a design requirement. Impact: late rework of measures and tests. Cause: Kestrel's under-5 rule sat in the classification register but was never turned into acceptance criteria. Recommendation: turn every privacy and security rule into a test case when requirements are written. Owner: Priya Raman (E-003). Applies to: Release 2 requirements, starting with the access-governance dashboard."

Candidate lessons from Beacon's own evidence:

| Topic | Evidence | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| Profiling first | 4 quarantined visits and 4 census problems found before modelling | Profile every Release 2 source first |
| Privacy as tests | D-02 condition; Coulee Valley Hospital (CVH) also had a count under 5 | Write suppression and row-level security (RLS) tests with the requirements |
| Calendar | No holidays in the schedule; Thanksgiving 2026-10-12 fell in Release 1 | Add statutory holidays, including Remembrance Day 2026-11-11 |
| Key person | Model knowledge sat with Tomás Rivera (R-06) | Pair Mei Tanaka on every model change |
| Cost | Release 1 CPI 0.89 | Re-estimate Release 2 with Release 1 actuals |

Run it with the team and keep it blameless: ask what in the process allowed the outcome.

read.heading: PL-300 coverage review: the four skill areas
read.body:
The PL-300 exam lasts 100 minutes and needs a scaled score of 700 to pass. It measures four skill areas:

| Skill area | Weight | Where Beacon practised it |
|---|---|---|
| Prepare the data | 25–30% | Power Query data-quality workbook and quality plan (weeks 1 and 3) |
| Model the data | 25–30% | Star schema, date table and Data Analysis Expressions (DAX) catalogue (week 4) |
| Visualize and analyze the data | 25–30% | Executive and site operations reports (week 5) |
| Manage and secure Power BI | 15–20% | RLS test pack; workspace, refresh and deployment plan (weeks 4 and 5) |

Rate yourself 1 to 3 on each area: 3 means you could teach it, 2 means you recognize it, 1 means it is new. Then test the rating against evidence: your recent PL-300 answers in Practice and the documents you completed. Feelings are not evidence. Every topic you rate 1 goes on the study list for the next two sessions.

A real project never touches every exam topic, so the next two sections teach the preparation and modelling topics Beacon did not need.

read.heading: Prepare the data: topics Beacon did not exercise
read.body:
- Storage modes: Import copies data into the model (fast, needs refresh). DirectQuery sends queries to the source when people view the report (current data; the source carries the load; some features are limited). Direct Lake, in Microsoft Fabric, reads Delta tables in OneLake directly, close to Import speed without a full import refresh. A composite model mixes modes.
- Data source settings: change credentials and privacy levels (Private, Organizational, Public, None). Privacy levels stop data from one source being sent to another when a query combines them.
- Parameters: an Environment or ServerName parameter lets one query point at Development or Production; deployment rules can set it per stage.
- Column profiling: Column quality, Column distribution and Column profile use the first 1,000 rows by default. Switch to the entire data set before you trust them.
- Reference or duplicate: Reference starts a new query from the original's output, so later changes flow through. Duplicate copies every step into an independent query.
- Merge and append: merge joins columns from two queries on matching keys (left outer, right outer, full outer, inner, left anti, right anti). Append stacks rows of queries with the same columns. A left anti merge finds orphans, such as tickets whose site has no match.
- Pivot, unpivot and transpose: unpivot turns columns into attribute and value rows (a census sheet with one column per unit becomes one row per unit per day); pivot reverses it; transpose swaps rows and columns.
- Loading: turn off Enable load for staging queries so they do not become model tables.

read.heading: Model the data: topics Beacon did not exercise
read.body:
- Role-playing dimension: one dimension related to a fact table more than once. Suppose you add FactEDVisit[DepartureDate] = DateTime.Date([DepartureDateTime]) and a second relationship from DimDate[Date]. Only one relationship can be active; a measure turns on the inactive one:

```
ED Visits by Departure Date =
CALCULATE (
    [ED Visits],
    USERELATIONSHIP ( DimDate[Date], FactEDVisit[DepartureDate] )
)
```

- Cross-filter direction: keep one-to-many, single direction from dimension to fact; both directions only for a known need, as it can create ambiguity.
- Calculation groups: reusable calculation items applied to any measure through SELECTEDMEASURE. Adding one switches on the setting that discourages implicit measures, so every value must come from an explicit measure.

```
YTD = CALCULATE ( SELECTEDMEASURE (), DATESYTD ( DimDate[Date] ) )
```

- Calculated column or measure: a column is computed row by row at refresh and stored; a measure is computed at query time in the filter context. Use a column when you must slice or filter by the value.
- Quick measures build common patterns, such as running totals, from a dialog.
- Semi-structured data (Prepare): expand JSON records into columns and lists into rows.
- Statistical functions: MEDIAN, MEDIANX, PERCENTILEX.INC and STDEV.S. A 90th percentile wait is PERCENTILEX.INC over visits with a valid MinutesToPIA.
- Optimize: remove unused columns, reduce granularity (a date, not a date and time), and turn off Auto date/time once you have a marked date table.

Confirming a release's acceptance and handover, scheduling benefit measurement, and moving open risks, issues and contracts to named owners while the programme continues.
A dimension, such as a date table, related to one fact table more than once. One relationship is active; the others are inactive and used through USERELATIONSHIP.
A model object holding reusable calculation items, such as year to date, that apply to any measure through SELECTEDMEASURE. It requires explicit measures.
A Microsoft Fabric storage mode in which the semantic model reads Delta tables in OneLake directly, without importing a copy on a refresh schedule.

Reference keeps a query linked to the original's output; Duplicate makes an independent copy. To find unmatched keys between two tables, use a left anti merge.
